rv.q: The cast oozed talent, notably Tony Actresses Montego Glover and Stephanie J. Block, who portray the Witch and the Baker's Wife respectively.
It's simultaneously spare and sumptuous, tart and tender.
With such a wealth of world-class talent, it's difficult to single out standouts among this enchanted ensemble.
At the center of all this wonder is Montego Glover's electrifying performance as the Witch.

With a cast of Broadway veterans (Stephanie J. Block has been out as the Baker’s Wife since the show opened here; Ximone Rose took the role Friday night) and an onstage orchestra, deBessonet’s staging brings a clarity to the ancient fairy tales Sondheim reshaped and merged (with book writer James Lapine) into a haunting meditation on love, loss,...
It’s worth noting that this production started its life as a concert, and as such is fairly minimal in its execution. A base set and an onstage orchestra are all we really get in terms of thrills.
